defects.justification: readBody calls getRequestBody().readAllBytes() with no size cap, so any client (including the public /orgs, /login and /invitations/accept routes) can make the server buffer an arbitrarily large body in memory.
The JDK HttpServer is created with no executor (so it handles requests on a single dispatcher thread) and no read/request timeouts; one slow or stalled client blocks every other request.
POST /login has no attempt limiting, lockout or delay, so passwords (minimum length only 8) can be brute-forced online without restriction.

When the email is unknown, login returns 401 immediately without running the 120,000-iteration PBKDF2, while known emails pay the full hash cost; the response-time difference lets an attacker enumerate registered emails.
Session tokens are inserted with no expiry column and there is no logout or revocation path, so a leaked bearer token grants access to the organisation's notes forever.
Invitation tokens never expire and cannot be revoked by the admin; a leaked invitation (possibly carrying the admin role) stays usable indefinitely until accepted.
URLDecoder.decode throws IllegalArgumentException on a malformed percent escape (e.g. ?q=%zz); it is not mapped to 400 and falls through to the generic RuntimeException handler, returning 500.
